findings.evidence: nav element (id nav) contains exactly two links, 'Plan a trip' (href /plan) and 'Accessibility' (href /accessibility); no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail element appears anywhere else in the document
findings.violation: The page exposes only one navigation mechanism type, a two-link primary navigation menu, with no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail present anywhere, and nothing in the page marks it as one step in a linear process, so fewer than the two independent mechanisms WCAG-2.4.5 requires are present.
findings.fix: Add a second independent way to locate this page, such as a site search form, a sitemap link, or a breadcrumb trail reflecting the page's place in the site.

findings.evidence: heading text 'Fare adjustments'; the section it introduces also contains a control labeled 'Delete item' (aria-label), a three step sequence reading 'Choose a plan', 'Enter payment details', 'Confirm your order', and a signup form with Route, Email address, Phone number, and Promo code fields
findings.violation: The heading 'Fare adjustments' does not describe most of what follows it: a delete-item control, a three-step plan-and-payment sequence, and a Route, Email address, Phone number, and Promo code signup form, none of which a reader scanning the heading would predict.
findings.fix: Split the section by actual topic, for example a Fare adjustments subsection limited to the adjustment status text, with its own headings for the plan-and-payment sequence and for the signup form, or rewrite the heading to name everything the section covers.

findings.location: section s3, form, input id promo
findings.evidence: input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true" carries no aria-describedby; the adjacent span id="s3-form-promo-error" reads 'Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.' with nothing in either element linking the two
findings.violation: The promo code input is marked aria-invalid="true" but has no aria-describedby (or other programmatic association) pointing at the error-text span that follows it, so a screen-reader user who tabs to the field hears that it is invalid without hearing why.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to the promo input so its error text is announced together with the field.
